newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday and traders said an active and rising domestic A share market helped boost the repo rates with money demand increasing.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 10.70 percent from 10.30 percent on Monday.
Turnover fell slightly to 7.25 million lots from 7.98 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Major financial institutions borrowed money on the repo market today to speculate on the A share market, pushing up the rates, in particular early-maturing contracts," a trader said.
The listing of Hainan Overseas Chinese Investment Co today also helped the rates to go up, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up due to a report on the Shanghai Securities News which said Beijing was mulling a cut in loan interest rates, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, closed up at 121.86 yuan from 121.75 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 2.64 million lots from 3.15 million.
Traders expect the contracts to consolidate in a narrow range in the short term. - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
